pr.title: Feature flag: rolling-updates

raw_findings.body: The command now returns 3 for the recreate case and 4 for a completely different condition (feature disabled); existing scripts that branch on exit code 4 will misclassify "feature disabled" as "recreate required" and treat 3 as an unknown/unexpected code, breaking automation. The tool's stated purpose is to be "fully scriptable", so exit codes are the public API.
raw_findings.failure_mode: External scripts consuming the exit code take the wrong branch after upgrading, e.g., performing a recreate procedure when the feature flag is merely disabled.
raw_findings.impact: The command now returns 3 for the recreate case and 4 for a completely different condition (feature disabled); existing scripts that branch on exit code 4 will misclassify "feature disabled" as "recreate required" and treat 3 as an unknown/unexpected code, breaking automation. The tool's stated purpose is to be "fully scriptable", so exit codes are the public API.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch reassigns an already-shipped exit-code value to a new semantic (FEATURE_DISABLED) and moves the recreate semantic to a different value without a migration note.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep 4 as the recreate exit code and assign a new unused value (e.g., 5) to FEATURE_DISABLED, or explicitly document the exit-code renumbering as a breaking change in release notes/upgrade docs.
raw_findings.title: Renumbering RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 silently changes the scripted exit-code contract
raw_findings.trigger: A user or CI pipeline scripted against the previously shipped behavior (exit code 4 meant "recreate required") runs `update-compatibility check` against the new release when the metadata is incompatible.

raw_findings.body: The new constant reads as a state/flag rather than an exit code, obscuring that it belongs to the same exit-code enumeration and inviting misuse (e.g., as a boolean-like condition).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Reduced readability and inconsistent API surface in a type whose constants are consumed by multiple commands.
raw_findings.impact: The new constant reads as a state/flag rather than an exit code, obscuring that it belongs to the same exit-code enumeration and inviting misuse (e.g., as a boolean-like condition).
raw_findings.root_cause: New constant added without following the existing *_EXIT_CODE naming pattern declared on the immediately preceding lines.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the constant to FEATURE_DISABLED_EXIT_CODE to match the established suffix convention of the other exit-code constants in the same interface.
raw_findings.title: FEATURE_DISABLED constant breaks the *_EXIT_CODE naming convention of sibling constants
raw_findings.trigger: Any developer reading or extending CompatibilityResult, where the adjacent constants are ROLLING_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE and RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE.

raw_findings.body: The identical gating logic is copy-pasted into UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run(); a new or refactored subcommand can silently bypass the rolling-updates feature gate, and any change to the gate (message, exit code) must be made in multiple places.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Repeated-pattern drift: gates can diverge or be omitted in future subcommands, undermining the feature-flag enforcement.
raw_findings.impact: The identical gating logic is copy-pasted into UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run(); a new or refactored subcommand can silently bypass the rolling-updates feature gate, and any change to the gate (message, exit code) must be made in multiple places.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch places identical feature-gating code in each concrete command rather than in the shared abstract base that both already extend.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Move the gate into AbstractUpdatesCommand (e.g., a final run() template method that performs the feature check and delegates to an abstract doRun()), since printFeatureDisabled() already lives there.
raw_findings.title: Feature-gate block duplicated verbatim in both update subcommands instead of the shared base class
raw_findings.trigger: A future subcommand is added under `update-compatibility` (all such commands extend AbstractUpdatesCommand, which already hosts the shared printFeatureDisabled() helper) and the author forgets to copy this 5-line gate.

raw_findings.body: The exit codes newly documented in update-compatibility.adoc (m|3 recreate, m|4 feature disabled) are the scripting contract of this tool, yet nothing verifies them; a regression that returns the wrong code would pass CI while breaking every scripted consumer.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Undetected regressions in the documented exit-code contract that automation depends on.
raw_findings.impact: The exit codes newly documented in update-compatibility.adoc (m|3 recreate, m|4 feature disabled) are the scripting contract of this tool, yet nothing verifies them; a regression that returns the wrong code would pass CI while breaking every scripted consumer.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch introduces new externally documented exit-code behavior but the accompanying tests only assert stderr text, not the exit code.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Extend UpdateCommandDistTest to run the command via `distribution.run(...)` without the feature flag and assert `result.exitCode() == 4`, and assert exit code 3 in testWrongVersions.
raw_findings.title: No test asserts the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code 4 (or renumbered recreate code 3) is actually returned
raw_findings.trigger: Regression in Picocli.exit handling or in the exit-code constants (e.g., a future renumber) while running the existing dist test suite: UpdateCommandDistTest.testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message, and testWrongVersions only asserts error text, never exit codes 4 or 3.

raw_findings.body: The null check on the preceding lines implies pre-existing FeatureSpec contents should be preserved, but setEnabledFeatures replaces the whole list, silently dropping any previously enabled features and changing the deployment under test in a way the guard was written to avoid.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test setup silently discards prior feature configuration, producing a deployment that no longer matches the intended baseline if the base fixture ever sets features.
raw_findings.impact: The null check on the preceding lines implies pre-existing FeatureSpec contents should be preserved, but setEnabledFeatures replaces the whole list, silently dropping any previously enabled features and changing the deployment under test in a way the guard was written to avoid.
raw_findings.root_cause: Inconsistent mutation pattern: the patch preserves an existing FeatureSpec object but clobbers its enabledFeatures field.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Merge rather than replace: read the existing enabled-features list (defaulting to empty), append Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey(), and set the merged list.
raw_findings.title: UpgradeTest null-guards FeatureSpec but then unconditionally overwrites its enabled-features list
raw_findings.trigger: getTestKeycloakDeployment(true) (or a future change to it) returns a Keycloak CR that already carries a FeatureSpec with enabled features; createInitialDeployment then runs with a non-null update strategy.
